name: Business Weight Computation
description: Implement business weight calculation from its component metrics. Signal frequency: count of signals accepted per time window. Author seniority: average seniority score of signal authors (from identity resolver). Channel gravity: learned weight per source channel based on response patterns. Engagement velocity: rate of change of signal volume. Combine into a single [0.0, 1.0] score with floor of 0.1. Update periodically (during lifecycle checks). Async where identity resolver is needed. Module location: src/stigmergy/core/business_weight.py.

types.name: NormalizedScore
types.description: A float value clamped to [0.0, 1.0], representing a normalized sub-metric score. Annotated[float, Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)].

types.name: BusinessWeight
types.description: A float value in [0.1, 1.0], representing the composite business weight with a floor of 0.1 baked into the type. Annotated[float, Field(ge=0.1, le=1.0)].

types.name: BusinessWeightComponents

fields.name: signal_frequency
fields.description: Count of signals accepted in the time window, normalized to [0,1] via saturation divisor.

fields.name: author_seniority
fields.description: Average seniority score of signal authors resolved from identity resolver, normalized to [0,1]. Defaults to 0.5 when resolver is unavailable.

fields.name: channel_gravity
fields.description: Learned per-channel weight based on historical response patterns, normalized to [0,1]. Defaults to 0.5 when no learned weight is available for the channel.

fields.name: engagement_velocity
fields.description: Rate of change of signal volume over the time window, squashed to [0,1] via sigmoid or similar monotonic function.

fields.name: composite
fields.description: Final weighted linear combination of the four sub-metrics, normalized and floored at 0.1. This is the value written to context.business_weight.

fields.name: defaulted_metrics
fields.description: Names of sub-metrics that used fallback/default values rather than resolved values. Used for observability and debugging. Valid names: 'signal_frequency', 'author_seniority', 'channel_gravity', 'engagement_velocity'.

types.description: Frozen Pydantic v2 model holding four normalized sub-metric scores, the composite business weight, and a frozenset of metric names that fell back to defaults. Immutable after construction for safe sharing across async boundaries.

types.name: FrozenSetStr
types.description: A frozenset of strings. Represented as list<str> in the contract type system but implemented as frozenset[str] in Python for immutability.

fields.name: engagement_velocity

types.description: Relative weights for the four sub-metrics used in the weighted linear combination. Values do not need to sum to 1.0; they are normalized internally.

types.name: BusinessWeightConfig

fields.name: metric_weights
fields.description: Relative weights for the four sub-metrics in the weighted linear combination.

fields.name: window_seconds
fields.description: Time window in seconds over which signal_frequency and engagement_velocity are computed.

fields.name: frequency_saturation
fields.description: Maximum expected signal count within the time window. Used to normalize raw signal count to [0,1]. signal_frequency = min(raw_count / frequency_saturation, 1.0).

fields.name: default_weight
fields.description: Default business weight value used before first computation and as fallback for sub-metrics when resolution fails.

fields.name: floor
fields.description: Minimum composite business weight. The composite is clamped to max(computed, floor).

fields.name: seniority_timeout_seconds
fields.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the identity resolver to return author seniority before falling back to default.

functions.name: compute_business_weight
functions.description: Pure synchronous function that computes a BusinessWeightComponents from four raw sub-metric float inputs. Performs clamping of all inputs to [0.0, 1.0], weighted linear combination using the provided MetricWeights, normalization, and flooring at the configured minimum. No I/O, no side effects, fully testable. This is the core scoring logic.

inputs.name: signal_frequency
inputs.description: Raw signal frequency value. Will be clamped to [0.0, 1.0] internally.

inputs.name: author_seniority
inputs.description: Raw author seniority score. Will be clamped to [0.0, 1.0] internally.

inputs.name: channel_gravity
inputs.description: Raw channel gravity weight. Will be clamped to [0.0, 1.0] internally.

inputs.name: engagement_velocity
inputs.description: Raw engagement velocity value. Will be clamped to [0.0, 1.0] internally.

inputs.name: weights
inputs.description: Relative weights for the four sub-metrics. Normalized internally so they sum to 1.0. Defaults to MetricWeights() which provides (0.25, 0.30, 0.25, 0.20).

inputs.name: floor
inputs.description: Minimum composite value. Composite is clamped to max(computed, floor).

inputs.name: defaulted_metrics
inputs.description: Set of metric names that used fallback values, passed through to the result for observability.

error_cases.name: non_finite_input
error_cases.condition: Any input float is NaN or Inf

error_data.field: name of the non-finite input parameter

error_cases.name: all_zero_weights
error_cases.condition: All four weight values in MetricWeights are 0.0, making normalization impossible

error_data.detail: All metric weights are zero; cannot normalize

error_cases.name: invalid_floor
error_cases.condition: floor is negative or greater than 1.0

preconditions: All input floats are finite (not NaN, not Inf)
weights has at least one non-zero weight value
postconditions: result.composite == max(floor, weighted_sum / sum_of_weights) where weighted_sum uses clamped inputs
All sub-metric fields are clamped versions of corresponding inputs

functions.name: resolve_business_weight
functions.description: Async wrapper that resolves all sub-metric inputs from external dependencies and signal history, then delegates to compute_business_weight(). Fetches author seniority from the identity resolver with a configurable timeout and fallback to default. Computes signal_frequency by counting signals in the time window normalized by frequency_saturation. Computes engagement_velocity from the rate of change of signal volume across window halves. Looks up channel_gravity from learned channel weights map. Returns the full BusinessWeightComponents for observability. Does NOT mutate context.business_weight — the caller (lifecycle check) is responsible for assignment.

inputs.name: context
inputs.description: The Context/WorkerNode whose business weight is being computed. Provides context_id and channel for lookups.

inputs.name: identity_resolver
inputs.description: Async identity resolver providing author seniority scores. Called with timeout; falls back to config.default_weight on failure.

inputs.name: channel_weights
inputs.description: Learned channel gravity weights map. Used to look up gravity for context.channel.

inputs.name: signal_history
inputs.description: List of signal records within the relevant time window. Used to compute signal_frequency and engagement_velocity.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration controlling weights, time windows, saturation, defaults, floor, and timeout.

error_cases.name: identity_resolver_timeout
error_cases.condition: Identity resolver does not respond within config.seniority_timeout_seconds

error_cases.name: identity_resolver_error
error_cases.condition: Identity resolver raises an unexpected exception during seniority resolution

error_data.original_error: string representation of the original exception

error_cases.name: invalid_signal_history
error_cases.condition: signal_history contains records with non-finite or negative timestamps

preconditions: identity_resolver implements the resolve_seniority async protocol
signal_history timestamps are Unix epoch floats
postconditions: result.defaulted_metrics contains names of all metrics that used fallback values
If identity_resolver times out or fails, 'author_seniority' is in result.defaulted_metrics and result.author_seniority == config.default_weight
If context.channel is not in channel_weights.weights, 'channel_gravity' is in result.defaulted_metrics
If signal_history is empty, 'signal_frequency' and 'engagement_velocity' are in result.defaulted_metrics
side_effects: Calls identity_resolver.resolve_seniority() which may involve network I/O
May emit observability/logging events for defaulted metrics and timeout fallbacks

functions.name: compute_signal_frequency
functions.description: Pure helper function that computes the normalized signal frequency from a signal history and configuration. Counts signals within the time window and divides by frequency_saturation, clamping to [0.0, 1.0].

inputs.name: signal_history
inputs.description: List of signal records to count within the window.

inputs.name: window_seconds
inputs.description: Time window in seconds. Only signals within [now - window_seconds, now] are counted.

inputs.name: frequency_saturation
inputs.description: Maximum expected signal count for normalization.

inputs.name: now
inputs.description: Current Unix timestamp for windowing. Allows deterministic testing.

error_data.detail: window_seconds and frequency_saturation must be positive

preconditions: now is a valid finite Unix timestamp

functions.name: compute_engagement_velocity
functions.description: Pure helper function that computes the engagement velocity from signal history. Splits the time window into two halves, counts signals in each half, and computes the rate of change as (recent_count - older_count) / max(older_count, 1), squashed through a sigmoid-like function to [0.0, 1.0].

inputs.name: signal_history
inputs.description: List of signal records for velocity computation.

inputs.name: window_seconds
inputs.description: Total time window in seconds. Split into two equal halves.

inputs.name: now
inputs.description: Current Unix timestamp for windowing. Allows deterministic testing.

preconditions: now is a valid finite Unix timestamp
postconditions: If signal volume is constant across halves, result == 0.5 (neutral velocity)
Increasing volume yields result > 0.5, decreasing volume yields result < 0.5

functions.name: lookup_channel_gravity
functions.description: Pure helper function that looks up the channel gravity weight from the learned channel weights map. Returns the default gravity if the channel is not found in the map.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Channel identifier to look up.

inputs.name: channel_weights
inputs.description: Learned channel gravity weights map.

postconditions: If channel is in channel_weights.weights, result == clamp(channel_weights.weights[channel], 0.0, 1.0)
If channel is not in channel_weights.weights, result == channel_weights.default_gravity

identity_resolver: Provides async resolve_seniority(author_id: str) -> float returning a NormalizedScore in [0.0, 1.0]
Must respond within configurable timeout (default 2.0 seconds)
May raise exceptions on network failures which are caught and handled with fallback

invariants: compute_business_weight is a pure function: same inputs always produce the same output, no side effects
The composite field is always >= the configured floor (minimum 0.1)
The composite field is always a weighted linear combination of the four sub-metrics, normalized and floored
MetricWeights are normalized internally; callers do not need to ensure they sum to 1.0
resolve_business_weight never raises on identity resolver failures; it falls back to default and records in defaulted_metrics
The context.business_weight field remains in [0.1, 1.0] at all times after initialization
Default business weight is 0.5 before first computation
defaulted_metrics only contains values from the set {'signal_frequency', 'author_seniority', 'channel_gravity', 'engagement_velocity'}
requires: identity_resolver must be available at runtime for author seniority resolution
Signal history must be maintained externally and passed to resolve_business_weight
Channel weights map must be learned and maintained externally (e.g., from response pattern analysis)
Lifecycle checks must call resolve_business_weight periodically and assign result.composite to context.business_weight
